component: Comparison and mutation probes; optional-backend test boundaries
constraints: Bounded developer/CI diagnostics for trusted local source and fixed synthetic fixtures. No service deadline, embedded target or throughput SLA.
Dependency-free core jobs must retain independent checks and report unavailable crypto coverage explicitly. Dedicated passport jobs install and import the required backend before testing.
alternatives: Python asyncio capture and unittest fixtures invoking native-backed Python crypto and the exact runtime API.
Node.js/TypeScript child-process orchestration and native crypto comparison.
C#/F# System.Diagnostics.Process for external probe supervision.
Rust native process orchestration with independently defined Python report contracts.
rationale: KEEP comparison observer in Python and Node primitive comparator: direct runtime observations and explicit lexical differences matter; neither primitive speed nor one desktop batch establishes a replacement verifier.

KEEP mutation runner in Python: it compiles isolated copies of the actual Python verifier and executes existing real admission tests. A translated verifier or external orchestrator would not supply equivalent guard-sensitivity evidence by itself.

FIX test dependency declarations: only tests requiring positive crypto admission may skip in a missing-backend job. Floor persistence checks invoke their backend-independent scenario directly; core process controls and pinned-policy checks remain active.

Fresh no-site execution reproduced the CI failures, then passed 23 checks with 20 explicit dependency skips. With crypto installed, all 48 affected methods pass without skips. No alternative establishes a material advantage or winning migration under these constraints.
limits: Only Python and the Node primitive comparator were executed. C#/F# and Rust are architecture candidates, not measured performance results.
No-site skips are unavailable coverage, never crypto PASS. Probe executables still reject missing backend without success output.
Temporary module restoration and listed-source comparisons are not sandbox isolation or loaded-code attestation. Timers are local elapsed-time samples, not target qualification.
No hosted PASS is claimed for this correction. Three existing low-severity subprocess warnings in probe tests remain retained.
